abstract: Gestational trophoblastic disease (GTD) represents a spectrum of histologically distinct entities including molar pregnancy and choriocarcinoma. The incidence of GTD varies in different parts of the world with high incidences in countries like Japan (2 / 1000 pregnancies). With the advent of sensitive assays for detection of serum beta human chorionic gonadotrophin (HCG) and ultrasound, GTD can now be detected earlier in pregnancy. To date no studies have been reported from South Africa regarding the epidemiology, management, and outcome of patients with GTD. This study was a retrospective audit based on 112 patients with GTD treated at King Edward VIII Hospital, Durban, South Africa. Clinical records of patients were reviewed with regards to presentation, investigation, management and outcome. Of 112 patients, there were 78 patients (70%) with hydatidiform mole and 34 patients (30%) with choriocarcinoma. The mean age of patients was 28.5 years (SD 8.1 years). The majority of patients were Black females (94.6%) while 4.4% were Asian and 1% Coloured females. The most common presenting symptom was vaginal bleeding (93.8%). There were 74 patients (66.7%) who had a previous normal term pregnancy and only two patients (1.8%) had previous molar pregnancies. Suction curettage was the main treatment modality for patients with molar pregnancy while choriocarcinoma was treated primarily with chemotherapy. A total of 72 percent of patients with molar pregnancy and 28 percent with choriocarcinoma had complete remission after initial treatment. Twelve patients died during the course of treatment mainly due to late presentation and advanced metastatic disease. Complete cure was achieved in 89% of patients. Age, parity, previous history, initial uterine size, presence of theca-lutein cysts, and initial betaHCG concentration was not found to be prognostic for persistent trophoblastic disease. In the present study, the incidence of molar pregnancy and choriocarcinoma was 1.2 / 1000 and 0.5 / 1000 deliveries, respectively. This is much lower than those quoted from countries such as Japan. However, the incidence quoted from our study may be overestimated as this was a hospital-based study and most of the uncomplicated deliveries occur in referring centers. Only 20% of patients in this study were above the age of 35 years with a mean age of 28.5 years. The majority of patients were of Black African ethnic origin mainly due to the fact that our hospital is a referral center for Black patients. Similar to other studies, the majority of patients with molar pregnancy were treated with suction curettage while the majority of patients with choriocarcinoma were treated with chemotherapy. Overall, spontaneous remission was achieved in 60% of patients with molar pregnancy and an overall complete cure was achieved in 89% of patients.
abstract_ja:
妊娠性絨毛性疾患（GTD）は、胞状奇胎や絨毛癌を含む組織学的に異なる病型のスペクトラムを表す。GTDの発生率は地域によって異なり、日本のように高い発生率の国もある（妊娠1000件あたり2件）。感度の高い血清β-hCG測定法と超音波検査の普及により、妊娠中のGTDを早期に発見できるようになった。これまで南アフリカからはGTDの疫学、管理、転帰に関する報告がなかった。本研究は、南アフリカ・ダーバンのKing Edward VIII病院で治療された112例のGTD患者を対象とした後方視的監査である。患者の診療録を、初発症状、検査、管理、転帰について検討した。
112例のうち、78例（70%）が胞状奇胎、34例（30%）が絨毛癌であった。患者の平均年齢は28.5歳（標準偏差8.1歳）であった。大多数は黒人女性（94.6%）で、アジア系が4.4%、カラードの女性が1%であった。最も多い初発症状は性器出血（93.8%）であった。74例（66.7%）は以前に正常満期産の妊娠歴があり、以前に胞状奇胎妊娠歴があったのは2例（1.8%）のみであった。胞状奇胎患者の主な治療法は掻把術であり、絨毛癌は主に化学療法で治療された。初回治療後の完全寛解は、胞状奇胎患者の72%、絨毛癌患者の28%で得られた。治療中に12例が死亡したが、これは主に診断の遅れと進行した転移性疾患によるものであった。全体として89%の患者が完全治癒に至った。年齢、経産回数、既往歴、初診時の子宮の大きさ、卵巣黄体嚢胞の有無、初診時のβ-hCG濃度は、持続性栄養膜疾患の予後因子ではなかった。本研究では、胞状奇胎と絨毛癌の発生率は分娩1000件あたりそれぞれ1.2件と0.5件であった。これは日本などの国で報告されている値よりかなり低い。ただし、本研究は病院ベースの研究であり、大多数の正常分娩は紹介元の施設で行われているため、本研究の発生率は過大評価されている可能性がある。本研究の患者の平均年齢は28.5歳で、35歳以上は20%のみであった。大多数は黒人アフリカ系であったが、これは当院が黒人患者の紹介センターであることによる。他の研究と同様に、胞状奇胎患者の大多数は掻把術で、絨毛癌患者の大多数は化学療法で治療された。全体として、胞状奇胎患者の60%で自然寛解が得られ、全体の89%で完全治癒が得られた。
